**B01AF01** is the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification code for rivaroxaban, a direct oral anticoagulant ([[doac|DOAC]]) [^src1][^src3]. In the context of the Danish healthcare system's clinical quality databases, managed by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP), this code is essential for tracking medication usage and evaluating the quality of care for patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren]] [^src1][^src3]. 

Rivaroxaban (B01AF01) is specifically included in the clinical indicators used to measure [[antikoagulationsbehandling]] and the monitoring of renal function [^src1][^src2]. According to the national quality reports, anticoagulation therapy encompasses vitamin K antagonists ([[b01aa|B01AA]]) as well as several DOACs, explicitly listing B01AF01 (rivaroxaban) alongside [[b01ae07|B01AE07]] (dabigatran), [[b01af02|B01AF02]] (apixaban), and [[b01af03|B01AF03]] (edoxaban) [^src1]. 

The code appears in the technical methodologies and calculation rules for clinical quality indicators, serving as a standardized reference for data collection and comparison across Danish regions [^src2][^src3]. By defining precise ATC codes like B01AF01, the RKKP ensures that treatments and follow-ups for cardiovascular diseases are systematically recorded and evaluated [^src3].
